blocks.title: Server-timed booking model
blocks.text: A RentalSearch with branch-local times returns VehicleOffer snapshots, each with a server total and expiresAt. Reserve converts one offer into a VehicleHold through an idempotent command, and the countdown compares the hold's expiresAt with serverNow. Confirmation spends the live holdId once. A stale card, a returning tab or a late response only triggers a fresh offer or hold read.

blocks.title: Worked example: the hold expires during driver details

steps.title: Search
steps.text: The customer searches the San Francisco airport branch for pickup on 3 November at 10:00 and return on 6 November at 10:00, branch zone America/Los_Angeles. The URL carries both branch ids, the local times and the zone, so a shared link repeats the search.

steps.title: Choose
steps.text: Offer of_42 lists a compact SUV or similar for three rental days at 312.40 USD, airport fee included. The card shows the server total and adds nothing in the browser.

steps.title: Hold
steps.text: Reserve sends of_42 with key hk_1 and receives hold h_9. The coordinator records the offset between serverNow and the device clock and starts the countdown from it.

steps.title: Expire
steps.text: The customer steps away. The warning offers Keep holding before expiry, nobody answers, and the server expires h_9. The page moves to hold-expired and keeps every entered field.

steps.title: Re-hold
steps.text: Reserve again uses a new key, hk_2, because h_9 is terminal. The server answers price-changed with offer of_57 at 338.10 USD. The page shows both totals; after the customer accepts, Reserve sends of_57 with key hk_3 and hold h_10 leads to confirmation.

blocks.alt: Car rental booking flow from a branch-local browser search through server offers, an idempotent hold and a confirmed reservation, with payment in a separate provider.
blocks.caption: Authority flow: the browser carries intent, while offers, holds and the reservation come back from the rental backend.
blocks.fallbackText: Text fallback: The browser sends branch ids, local times and the zone. The backend returns priced offers with an expiry. Reserve creates a hold with an idempotency key, and confirmation spends that hold. Payment returns an opaque reference.
